12 / SIGNAL CLEANING
PerfuSense
BASELINE AND DRIFT, EXPLAINED.
BASELINE: SUBTRACT THE EMPTY MAT
Even an empty mat reads a little, and each cell differs. We record the empty mat at start and subtract it from every reading, so only real pressure remains.
Illustrative graph, not measured data.
DRIFT: VELOSTAT SLOWLY CREEPS
Under a constant load the resistance keeps changing slowly. Software correction and baseline resets when the mat is empty keep drift under 10%.
Curve shape illustrative; the end value, under 2% at 48 h, is measured.

13 / THE AI MODEL
PerfuSense
HOW WE BUILT THE AI, STEP BY STEP.
THE QUESTION
Can 30 seconds of a 10×10 mat tell supine, left side or right side?
01 AUDIT
Opened all 5 dataset downloads. Only 2 hold real data.
02 INSPECT
Plotted before training. Found broken frames, stillness and creep.
03 CLEAN
Removed 461 abnormal frames, leaving 19,563 clean frames.
04 PREPARE
Shrunk to 10×10, cut 30 s windows, scaled 0–1: 1,409 windows.
05 SPLIT
Divided by person, so the test is always on people never seen.
06 BUILD
Wrote a no-attention baseline and a Transformer from scratch.
07 TRAIN
Adam, class weights and early stopping on a laptop CPU.
08 TEST
Leave-one-person-out on all 13 people: 96% balanced accuracy.
Every number was measured by running our notebook · Data: PmatData [11][12][14]

Why balanced accuracy
Supine is 53% of the frames, so always answering “supine” scores 53% plain accuracy. Balanced accuracy counts each class equally, so guessing scores only 33%. We also report macro F1.

17 / DATA CHECKS
PerfuSense
LOOK BEFORE YOU TRAIN.
Broken startup frames
≈ 25×
normal pressure at the start of every file
Rule: drop frames above 3× or below ⅓ of the recording’s median. Removed 461 frames (2.3%).
People lie still
≈ 2.5%
mean change between frames
Order inside a 30 s window carries almost no information. This predicted the tie with the baseline.
Sensor creep
10–15%
slow rise over 80 s
Every soft mat creeps, including our Velostat mat. Per-window scaling removes most of it.

18 / PREPROCESSING
PerfuSense
FROM RAW FILES TO 1,409 WINDOWS.
1 LOAD
Text file to array, 2,048 numbers per row
(frames, 64, 32)
2 CLEAN
Drop startup and abnormal frames
19,563 frames
3 RESIZE
Area-average to 10×10; every sensor counts
(frames, 10, 10)
4 WINDOW
30 frames, stride 10: the 30 s the server will send
(30, 10, 10)
5 NORMALISE
Divide by the window’s 99th percentile, clip to 0–1
values 0 to 1
Why per-window scaling
Removes unit differences between mats and most creep. The same function must run on the server.
Our decision for now
The whole mat is shrunk to 10×10. Cropping the 30×30 cm patch our mat sees is a later step.

19 / HONEST TESTING
PerfuSense
SPLIT BY PERSON, NEVER RANDOMLY.
On the harder task a random split looks 19 points better than reality.
Neighbouring windows share 20 of their 30 frames, and a model can name who is lying down 81.8% of the time (chance 7.7%). A random split rewards that shortcut.

20 / MODEL STRUCTURE
PerfuSense
THE MODEL, LAYER BY LAYER.
Embedding 6,464
Attention 33,280
Feed-forward 33,152
Where the 75,651 parameters live · Time 1,920 · Norm and output 835
BASELINE · 6,659 PARAMETERS
No attention and no time. Average the 30 frames into one 10×10 picture, then Dense 64 (ReLU), Dropout 0.2, Dense 3. If the Transformer cannot beat this, attention is not helping.
TRANSFORMER · 75,651 PARAMETERS
Built from scratch in TensorFlow and Keras. Each frame is one token, like one word in a sentence. 11× bigger than the baseline and too big for the ESP32, so it runs on the server. The ESP32 keeps the simple pressure × time alarm.
Shapes in brackets · lower number in each box = parameters · Transformer [19]
21 / 40
21 / ENCODER BLOCK
PerfuSense
INSIDE ONE ENCODER BLOCK.
THE ATTENTION FORMULA
Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(Q·Kᵀ / √dₖ) · V
Each second looks at every other second and takes a weighted mix.
One block = 33,472 parameters. Dropout 0.1.
Our own code
Attention layer written by us, with the same 16,640 parameters as Keras’ built-in.
Pre-norm
LayerNorm comes before attention, for more stable training.
Learned positions
Attention alone ignores order. A shuffle test proved it.
Encoder only
Like BERT, not GPT. We classify and generate nothing, so no causal mask.
Lower number in each box = parameters · Multi-head self-attention [19]

Optimizer
Adam, learning rate 0.001
Batch size
32
Epochs
Up to 60, stops early (patience 8)
Class weights
Supine 0.63, left 1.42, right 1.42
Random seed
42, for repeatable runs
Augmentation
None yet
≈ 20 s
to train one Transformer
≈ 9 min
for all 26 models
How training behaved
Training accuracy reached 100% by epoch 3. Validation accuracy on new people stayed at 91–93%, and the best epoch was 8. The gap is overfitting to the training people, which early stopping limits.
Early stopping keeps the best weights · 26 models = 13 people × 2 models

29 / 40
29 / WHAT IT MEANS
PerfuSense
WHAT THE TIE TELLS US.
Transformer on S11–S13, 305 windows
Main mistake: right read as left (7). It would show the wrong side as unloaded.
1 A tie is a finding
11× bigger and not better: on still postures, attention over time does not help.
2 People differ
S10 and S13 are hardest for both models. Results move several points per person.
3 The full bed is too easy
Even a linear model gets about 100%. The real test is the 30×30 cm patch our mat sees.
4 Where attention should win
Recordings with real movement and turns, and turn events detected over time.
Single split: Transformer 95.6%, baseline 100%. Three people is small, so leave-one-person-out is the fair test.

HONEST LIMITS, NEXT AI STEPS.
HONEST LIMITS
Public accuracy is not our accuracy. Nothing here was measured on the Velostat mat.
Full-bed view. Our mat sees only 30×30 cm; expect lower scores.
Healthy volunteers lying still for 1–3 minutes. No patients and no real turns.
Only 13 people. Results move several points between people.
3 classes only. Prone and empty bed are not included yet.
Different sensors. Scaling reduces the gap but does not remove it.

Add PoPu-Data

Use synthetic data

Serve with FastAPI
